title: FLOWSTEP: A Framework for Learning to Predict GitHub Actions Workflow STEPs
title_zh: FLOWSTEP：学习预测GitHub Actions工作流步骤的框架

paragraphs.en: Continuous Integration and Delivery (CI/CD) are fundamental to modern software development, yet configuring pipelines such as GitHub Actions (GHA) workflows remains complex and error-prone. Recent work has explored Transformer-based models for GHA workflow recommendation, but existing approaches typically model workflow steps as a single homogeneous generation task. This formulation overlooks a key distinction: reusable Actions are structured, ecosystem-level components, whereas project-specific Scripts encode local build, test, and deployment semantics. Consequently, current models struggle to capture the different forms of knowledge required for accurate workflow completion. In this work, we present FLOWSTEP , a framework for GHA workflow step completion that explicitly distinguishes between Action and Script generation. FLOWSTEP combines large language models (LLMs) with contrastive learning to better capture semantic relationships among workflow contexts, Actions, and Scripts. Evaluated on established benchmarks, FLOWSTEP improves end-to-end workflow step prediction accuracy from 38.23% to 51.09%. Beyond prediction accuracy, we further study whether LLM-as-a-judge can provide a more semantic evaluation of generated workflow steps. By comparing LLM-based assessments with human annotations, we find that the best-performing model configuration reaches substantial agreement with human ground truth (Krippendorff’s α = 0.701 \alpha=0.701 ), suggesting that LLM-as-a-judge can serve as a scalable complement to manual evaluation.

paragraphs.en: GitHub has become the largest collaborative software ecosystem, connecting more than 180 million developers and hosting over 630 million repositories as of 2025 [ 1 ] . As projects grow, Continuous Integration and Delivery (CI/CD) has become essential for automating building, testing, and deployment [ 2 ] . To natively support these activities, GitHub launched GitHub Actions (GHA) [ 3 ] in November 2019, offering an integrated CI/CD environment directly within the platform. Within only 18 months, GHA surpassed Travis CI to become the most widely used automation framework on GitHub [ 4 ] . Its convenience and ecosystem of reusable components ( Actions ) have made workflow automation more accessible than ever.

paragraphs.en: Despite these advantages, configuring CI/CD pipelines remains challenging. Prior studies have repeatedly shown that developers struggle with pipeline setup, maintenance, and debugging [ 5 , 6 ] . In a survey by Saroar et al. [ 7 ] , about 60% of 90 participants reported difficulties when automating workflows using GHA, underscoring an urgent need for intelligent authoring support. While automated code assistance has seen breakthroughs in general programming tasks ( e.g., code completion [ 8 ] , assertion generation [ 9 ] , automated repair of vulnerabilities and bugs [ 10 , 11 ] ), workflow authoring introduces unique challenges. A CI/CD pipeline interleaves reusable Actions with free-form scripting and natural-language documentation, while embedding highly context-specific details such as directory paths or download URLs. These characteristics make workflow recommendation significantly harder than traditional code completion.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管有这些优势，配置 CI/CD 流水线仍然充满挑战。 以往研究反复表明，开发者在流水线的搭建、维护和调试方面困难重重 [ 5 , 6 ] 。 在 Saroar 等人的一项调查中， [ 7 ] ，90 名参与者中约有 60% 报告在使用 GHA 自动化工作流时遇到困难，凸显了对智能编写支持的迫切需求。 虽然自动化代码辅助在通用编程任务中已取得突破（例如代码补全 [ 8 ] 、断言生成 [ 9 ] 、漏洞与缺陷的自动修复 [ 10 , 11 ] ），但工作流编写带来了独特的挑战。 CI/CD 流水线将可复用的 Actions 与自由格式的脚本以及自然语言文档交织在一起，同时嵌入了高度依赖具体上下文的细节，例如目录路径或下载 URL。 这些特性使得工作流推荐的难度显著高于传统代码补全。

paragraphs.en: The rapid adoption of GHA has motivated learning-based workflow generation. Transformer models and LLMs have been used to synthesize or recommend workflow steps [ 12 , 13 ] , but existing approaches often treat steps as homogeneous generation targets. This overlooks the different prediction strategies required by Actions and shell Scripts : Actions require selecting a reusable identifier from the GHA ecosystem, whereas Scripts require generating project-specific shell commands from workflow context. Our analysis shows that this mismatch contributes to prediction errors and reduces robustness across heterogeneous workflow steps.
paragraphs.zh: GHA 的快速普及推动了基于学习的 workflow 生成。 Transformer 模型和大语言模型已被用于合成或推荐 workflow 步骤 [ 12 , 13 ] ，但现有方法往往将步骤视为同质的生成目标。 这忽略了 Actions 和 shell 脚本所需的不同预测策略：Actions 需要从 GHA 生态中选出一个可复用的标识符，而 shell 脚本则需要根据 workflow 上下文生成项目特定的 shell 命令。 我们的分析表明，这种不匹配会导致预测错误，并降低在异构 workflow 步骤上的鲁棒性。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we address the problem of recommending the next step in GHA workflows, accounting for the heterogeneous nature of workflow steps. To this end, we propose FLOWSTEP , a multi-step prediction framework comprising (i) a binary classifier that predicts whether the next step is an Action or a Script , (ii) a RoBERTa model with contrastive learning that predicts the specific Action , and (iii) an LLM that generates the step when it is a Script . For comparability with prior work, we use the GHA workflow corpus by Decan et al. [ 14 ] , further processed by Mastropaolo et al. [ 12 ] into two variants: a raw version preserving original content and an abstracted version replacing project-specific tokens (e.g., paths) with placeholders while retaining commands and tool options. We evaluate FLOWSTEP on both variants to assess robustness across data granularities. The next step is predicted from the preceding workflow context concatenated with the step’s descriptive name, reflecting real workflow authoring scenarios.
paragraphs.zh: 在本工作中，我们研究在 GHA 工作流中推荐下一步的问题，并考虑工作流步骤的异构性。 为此，我们提出 FLOWSTEP，一个多步骤预测框架，包括：(i) 一个二分类器，用于预测下一步是 Action 还是 Script；(ii) 一个采用对比学习的 RoBERTa 模型，用于预测具体的 Action；(iii) 一个 LLM，用于在下一步为 Script 时生成该步骤。 为了与先前工作具有可比性，我们使用 Decan 等人的 GHA 工作流语料库 [ 14 ]，该语料库经 Mastropaolo 等人 [ 12 ] 进一步处理为两种变体：保留原始内容的原始版本，以及将项目特定标记（例如路径）替换为占位符同时保留命令和工具选项的抽象化版本。 我们在两种变体上评估 FLOWSTEP，以考察其在不同数据粒度下的稳健性。 下一步是通过将前置工作流上下文与该步骤的描述性名称拼接来进行预测的，这反映了真实的工作流编写场景。

paragraphs.en: The main contributions of our study are as follows:

paragraphs.en: We formulate GHA workflow step recommendation as a heterogeneous prediction problem and present FLOWSTEP , a step-type-aware framework that differentiates reusable Actions from project-specific Scripts , improving prediction accuracy from 38.23% to 51.09% (raw data).
paragraphs.zh: 我们将 GHA 工作流步骤推荐构建为一个异构预测问题，并提出了 FLOWSTEP，这是一个步骤类型感知的框架，能够区分可复用的 Actions 与项目特定的 Scripts，将预测准确率从 38.23% 提升至 51.09%（原始数据）。

paragraphs.en: We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of different model configurations for FLOWSTEP . Combining a RoBERTa-based model for Action prediction with Claude-Sonnet-4.5 for Script generation yields the best performance.
paragraphs.zh: 我们对 FLOWSTEP 的不同模型配置进行了全面评估。 将基于 RoBERTa 的模型用于动作预测，并结合 Claude-Sonnet-4.5 进行脚本生成，可获得最佳性能。

paragraphs.en: Each workflow contains one or more jobs , representing independent execution units that run on GitHub-hosted or self-hosted runners . Jobs may run concurrently or sequentially, and they remain isolated unless they explicitly share artifacts or caches. Each job consists of a series of steps , the smallest executable elements in a workflow. Steps can be defined either with the run keyword to execute shell commands ( Scripts ) directly within the runner (e.g., gradle build ) or with the uses keyword to invoke reusable Actions [ 16 ] . Script -based steps are preferred for simple or project-specific tasks, whereas Actions encapsulate recurring operations and can be versioned for reproducibility (e.g., actions/checkout@v3 ). Through this declarative structure, GHA provides a unified mechanism to automate CI/CD pipelines directly within GitHub repositories.

paragraphs.en: The evolution of Transformer architectures [ 17 ] and encoders like BERT [ 18 ] has enabled models to learn deep contextual representations of text and code. RoBERTa [ 19 ] , a refinement of BERT, employs dynamic masking and achieves more stable and robust performance across various Natural Language Processing tasks. Contrastive learning [ 20 ] further improves representation learning by introducing pairwise comparison, encouraging similar examples (positive pairs) to align closely in the embedding space while separating dissimilar ones (negative pairs). Given a batch of samples, an encoder transforms each input into a latent vector, and a similarity function ( e.g., cosine similarity) quantifies pairwise closeness. The resulting contrastive loss enhances semantic discrimination, which we leverage to fine-tune RoBERTa for more context-aware and task-specific representations in workflow step generation.
paragraphs.zh: Transformer 架构 [ 17 ] 以及 BERT [ 18 ] 等编码器的发展，使模型能够学习文本和代码的深层上下文表示。 RoBERTa [ 19 ] 是 BERT 的改进版本，采用动态掩码机制，在各类自然语言处理任务上实现了更加稳定和稳健的性能。 对比学习 [ 20 ] 通过引入成对比较进一步改进表示学习，鼓励相似样本（正样本对）在嵌入空间中紧密对齐，同时分离不相似的样本（负样本对）。 给定一批样本，编码器将每个输入转换为潜在向量，相似度函数（例如余弦相似度）用于量化样本对之间的接近程度。 由此得到的对比损失增强了语义区分能力，我们利用它对 RoBERTa 进行微调，以在生成工作流步骤时获得更具上下文感知能力和任务针对性的表示。

paragraphs.en: In recent years, LLMs have emerged as powerful tools capable of understanding and generating human-like text through extensive pre-training. Their versatility stems from the ability to generalize across diverse tasks using only textual instructions, without additional parameter updates. To further improve performance, researchers have proposed prompt engineering techniques [ 21 , 22 ] that carefully design input prompts to guide model behavior. Depending on the amount of task-specific context provided, LLM usage can be categorized into three settings [ 23 ] : (i) zero-shot , relying solely on pre-trained knowledge; (ii) one-shot , where a single example is provided; and (iii) few-shot , where multiple examples are given to refine responses. LLMs have transformed how developers interact with code, enabling natural-language-driven programming and automation. Models such as GPT-4 [ 24 ] , Claude-Sonnet [ 25 ] , CodeT5 [ 26 ] , and CodeBERT [ 27 ] demonstrate strong performance in code completion and synthesis. However, prior work largely focuses on general-purpose languages, leaving configuration artifacts underexplored. GHA workflows, written in YAML to define CI/CD automation, represent a distinct form of infrastructure configuration. Prior attempts to generate such workflows using fine-tuned T5 and LLMs [ 12 , 13 ] only partially capture workflow semantics, leading to limited accuracy and generalization. In this work, we guide LLMs to generate accurate and context-aware workflow steps for GHA automation.
paragraphs.zh: 近年来，大语言模型（LLMs）已成为强大的工具，能够通过大规模预训练来理解并生成类人的文本。 它们的通用性源于仅凭文本指令即可跨多样任务进行泛化的能力，而无需额外的参数更新。 为了进一步提升性能，研究者提出了提示工程（prompt engineering）技术 [ 21 , 22 ]，通过精心设计输入提示来引导模型行为。 根据所提供的任务特定上下文的数量，LLM 的使用可分为三种设置 [ 23 ]：(i) 零样本（zero-shot），仅依赖预训练知识；(ii) 单样本（one-shot），提供一个示例；(iii) 少样本（few-shot），提供多个示例以优化回答。 LLM 已经改变了开发者与代码交互的方式，实现了由自然语言驱动的编程与自动化。 GPT-4 [ 24 ]、Claude-Sonnet [ 25 ]、CodeT5 [ 26 ] 和 CodeBERT [ 27 ] 等模型在代码补全与代码生成方面展现了出色的性能。 然而，已有工作主要关注通用编程语言，对配置类制品的探索不足。 GHA 工作流以 YAML 编写、用于定义 CI/CD 自动化，代表了一种独特的基础设施配置形式。 此前使用微调的 T5 和 LLM 生成此类工作流的尝试 [ 12 , 13 ] 仅能部分捕捉工作流语义，导致准确性和泛化能力有限。 在本工作中，我们引导 LLM 为 GHA 自动化生成准确且具备上下文感知能力的工作流步骤。

paragraphs.en: Another emerging paradigm is LLM-as-a-Judge , which uses large language models as automatic evaluators of generated content instead of relying solely on human annotators. This idea builds on the observation that instruction-tuned models can reason about and compare outputs in a human-like manner [ 28 ] . Recent surveys [ 29 ] describe LLM-as-a-Judge as a scalable and cost-effective alternative to manual evaluation, although challenges such as bias, inconsistency, and over-alignment remain. In software engineering, recent studies [ 30 , 31 , 32 ] explore its use for automatically evaluating code and software artifacts, suggesting that with proper calibration, LLMs can complement human evaluators in domain-specific tasks.

paragraphs.en: The design of FLOWSTEP is motivated by an empirical analysis of the limitations in prior GHA recommendation models. Mastropaolo et al. [ 12 ] analyzed 384 workflow steps incorrectly predicted by their step prediction model GH-WCOM, and found that 159 recommendations were genuinely incorrect, while the remaining errors involved only minor issues. In this study, we further inspected these 159 erroneous predictions and found that 33.3% (53/159) are mismatches between Actions and Scripts , i.e., cases where an expected Action was replaced with a Script , or vice versa. For example, the step was predicted to be a script execution “ run: pip install tox ” while the developers adopted an existing Action “ uses: actions/cache@v1 ”.

paragraphs.en: Based on this, we hypothesize that explicitly distinguishing between Action and Script steps can improve the recommendation accuracy by preventing a single model from conflating two different prediction spaces. Therefore, we implement a Step-Type Predictor based on a RoBERTa encoder, mapping a workflow context ( i.e., input_context ) to a contextualized representation. This representation is passed through a dropout layer and a fully connected layer to perform binary classification of step type ( 1 1 : Action , 0 0 : Script ). paragraphs.zh: 基于此，我们假设明确区分 Action 和 Script 两类步骤可以避免单一模型混淆两种不同的预测空间，从而提升推荐的准确性。 因此，我们实现了一个基于 RoBERTa 编码器的步骤类型预测器（Step-Type Predictor），将工作流上下文（即 input_context）映射为上下文相关的表示。 该表示经过一个 dropout 层和一个全连接层，用于对步骤类型进行二分类（1: Action，0: Script）。 RoBERTa 模型使用 Hugging Face 的预训练权重进行初始化，并采用带 Logits 的二元交叉熵损失进行微调。

sents.en: During model development, the context encoder and classification head are trained in two distinct phases:

paragraphs.en: Phase 1: Contrastive training of the context encoder. We fine-tune RoBERTa using a contrastive objective that combines N-pair Loss and Soft-Nearest Neighbor Loss [ 33 ] . For each Action instance, we pair its workflow context with another context using the same Action as a positive example, while contexts using different Actions in the same batch serve as negative examples. This encourages contexts that require the same reusable Action to be close in the embedding space and separates contexts associated with different Actions ; implementation details and the full loss formulation are provided in our replication package.
paragraphs.zh: 阶段一：上下文编码器的对比训练。 我们使用结合了 N-pair 损失与软最近邻损失 [33] 的对比目标对 RoBERTa 进行微调。 对于每个 Action 实例，我们将其工作流上下文与使用同一 Action 的另一个上下文配对作为正例，而同一批次中使用不同 Action 的上下文则作为负例。 这促使需要相同可复用 Action 的上下文在嵌入空间中彼此接近，并使与不同 Action 相关的上下文相互分离；实现细节与完整的损失公式见我们的复现包。

paragraphs.en: Unlike Actions , Script steps offer greater flexibility, making them more error-prone and harder to predict. Since modern LLMs are good at code generation and Scripts essentially consist of shell commands, we leverage LLMs to generate executable workflow Scripts .

paragraphs.en: Calibration set. A small but representative calibration set D C ​ a ​ l ​ i D_{Cali} of 1,000 randomly sampled test instances from D S ​ c ​ r ​ i ​ p ​ t D_{Script} was used for comparative analysis to identify the most effective model and prompting configuration. Generated steps were compared against reference steps ( i.e., target_step ) using accuracy and n-gram based metrics (BLEU-4, ROUGE-L). The LLM with the best performance on D C ​ a ​ l ​ i D_{Cali} is selected as the final Script Generator. Our results show that Claude-Sonnet-4.5 with one-shot prompting performs best; thus, it is used as the Script Generator in FLOWSTEP .

sents.zh: RQ 1：FLOWSTEP 在为 GitHub Actions 工作流生成准确推荐方面效果如何？

sents.en: This RQ examines whether the steps recommended by FLOWSTEP align with those originally created by developers, using the previously proposed workflow completion model, GH-WCOM, as a baseline for comparison.
sents.zh: 该 RQ 考察 FLOWSTEP 推荐的步骤是否与开发者最初创建的步骤一致，并采用先前提出的工作流补全模型 GH-WCOM 作为对比基线。

paragraphs.en: RQ 2 : What is the impact of different model configurations within the FLOWSTEP framework on its final performance? The architecture of FLOWSTEP is based on a “divide-and-conquer” strategy that separates Action and Script generation. This RQ focuses on isolating the design choices of our framework through a series of ablation studies. We aim to quantify the contribution of each component to the overall performance of FLOWSTEP .
paragraphs.zh: RQ 2：FLOWSTEP 框架内不同的模型配置对其最终性能有何影响？ FLOWSTEP 的架构基于「分而治之」的策略，将动作与脚本生成相分离。 该 RQ 旨在通过一系列消融实验来隔离本框架的各项设计选择。 我们旨在量化每个组件对 FLOWSTEP 整体性能的贡献。

sents.en: RQ 2 : What is the impact of different model configurations within the FLOWSTEP framework on its final performance?

paragraphs.en: To ensure comparability with prior work, we use the dataset established by Mastropaolo et al. [ 12 ] for GH-WCOM. The dataset contains 73,708 GHA workflows collected by Decan et al. [ 14 ] and 733 additional workflows mined from 1,124 repositories by Mastropaolo et al. Their preprocessing removed duplicates, filtered workflows exceeding 1,024 tokens, and excluded non-ASCII instances, resulting in 17,935 unique workflows. Workflows are represented as JSON-like objects to preserve their structure. From these workflows, we construct step-level instances for the prediction task. Each step-level instance is represented as a tuple (input_context, target_step, type_step) , as mentioned in Section III .
paragraphs.zh: 为确保与先前工作的可比性，我们使用 Mastropaolo 等人 [12] 为 GH-WCOM 建立的数据集。 该数据集包含由 Decan 等人收集的 73,708 个 GHA 工作流。 [14] 以及 Mastropaolo 等人从 1,124 个仓库中挖掘出的 733 个额外工作流。 他们的预处理去除了重复项，过滤了超过 1,024 个 token 的工作流，并排除了非 ASCII 实例，最终得到 17,935 个唯一工作流。 工作流以类 JSON 对象的形式表示，以保留其结构。 我们从这些工作流中构建步骤级实例用于预测任务。 如第 III 节所述，每个步骤级实例表示为一个元组 (input_context, target_step, type_step)。

paragraphs.en: To address RQ 1 , we evaluate the best-performing configuration of FLOWSTEP on the test sets. For each test instance, FLOWSTEP generates the next workflow step based on the preceding workflow context, and the generated step is compared with the reference step from the original workflow. The overall performance is measured using exact-match accuracy, defined as the proportion of cases where the generated step exactly matches the reference step. To further analyze FLOWSTEP , we evaluate its three sub-models separately on their respective prediction tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 为回答研究问题1（RQ 1），我们在测试集上评估FLOWSTEP表现最佳的配置。 对于每个测试实例，FLOWSTEP根据前序工作流上下文生成下一个工作流步骤，并将生成的步骤与原始工作流中的参考步骤进行比较。 整体性能使用精确匹配准确率来衡量，该准确率定义为生成步骤与参考步骤完全一致的案例所占比例。 为了进一步分析FLOWSTEP，我们分别在其各自的预测任务上评估其三个子模型。

The predicted step types are then used to route each instance to either Action Predictor ( M A M_{A} ) or Script Generator ( M S M_{S} ) for the subsequent step prediction.
paragraphs.zh: 对于步骤类型预测器（ M T M_{T} ），我们报告准确率，其定义为被正确分类的步骤类型所占的比例。 预测出的步骤类型随后被用于将每个实例路由到动作预测器（ M A M_{A} ）或脚本生成器（ M S M_{S} ），以进行后续的步骤预测。

paragraphs.en: To answer RQ 2 , we investigate how different components and design choices affect the overall performance of FLOWSTEP . We first examine the core design choice of explicitly distinguishing between Action and Script steps to determine whether this separation improves prediction performance. Specifically, we conduct an error analysis of the baseline model GH-WCOM to identify mispredictions associated with incorrect step-type classification. We then evaluate to what extent FLOWSTEP reduces such errors by introducing a dedicated M T M_{T} for step-type prediction.
paragraphs.zh: 为回答研究问题2，我们研究不同组件和设计选择如何影响FLOWSTEP的整体性能。 我们首先考察显式区分动作步骤和脚本步骤这一核心设计选择，以确定这种区分是否能提升预测性能。 具体而言，我们对基线模型GH-WCOM进行错误分析，以识别与错误步骤类型分类相关的误预测。 然后我们评估FLOWSTEP通过引入专用于步骤类型预测的M T M_{T}在多大程度上减少了此类错误。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate M A M_{A} and its two variants on the test set of D A ​ c ​ t ​ i ​ o ​ n D_{Action} using Top- K K accuracy [ 36 ] , which measures whether the ground-truth action appears among the top- K K recommendations ( K = 1 K=1 – 5 5 ).

paragraphs.en: We conduct an ablation study comparing M A M_{A} with its two variants ( No-classification head and No-contrastive ), evaluated using Top- K K accuracy on D A ​ c ​ t ​ i ​ o ​ n D_{Action} . Table V reports the results of the M A M_{A} variants on both abstracted and raw datasets, using GH-WCOM as the baseline. Without contrastive learning, the model yields poor performance (Top-1: 21.51%/23.37%, Top-5: 50.30%/52.49%), showing that standard fine-tuning alone is insufficient for accurate Action prediction. Introducing contrastive learning leads to substantial improvements, increasing Top-1 performance to 80.05%/83.57% and Top-5 to 89.11%/91.26%. Adding the classification head further improves Top-1 by 7.18%/4.51% and Top-5 by 5.52%/2.91%, with diminishing gains as K K increases. This trend is consistent across both abstracted and raw datasets, and the full model substantially outperforms GH-WCOM. Overall, contrastive learning accounts for most of the performance gain, while the classification head provides additional improvements, particularly for Top-1 accuracy. The high Top-5 accuracy of the full model (94.63%/94.17%) further shows that M A M_{A} can provide a compact ranked set of plausible reusable Actions , which is useful when the top-ranked prediction is not correct but the correct Action remains among the leading candidates.

paragraphs.en: We further compare LLM-based judges with traditional automatic metrics ( i.e., BLEU and ROUGE). Since all 350 samples in this experiment correspond to incorrect script snippets, the accuracy is always zero and therefore not meaningful for comparison. To examine how well different evaluation approaches reflect human judgment, we compute the Spearman correlation ρ \rho between each metric and the human ground-truth. As shown in Table VIII , BLEU achieves a moderate correlation with human labels ( ρ = 0.514 \rho=0.514 ), while ROUGE reaches a stronger correlation ( ρ = 0.692 \rho=0.692 ). The five LLM judges achieve correlations ranging from 0.382 0.382 to 0.703 0.703 across zero-shot and one-shot settings. In the zero-shot setting, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp achieves the highest correlation ( ρ = 0.703 \rho=0.703 ), while in the one-shot setting GPT-4.1 performs best ( ρ = 0.695 \rho=0.695 ). These results suggest that the best-performing LLM-judge configurations match or slightly exceed widely used lexical-overlap metrics in their alignment with human judgment, while additionally assessing the functional correctness of generated scripts.

paragraphs.en: To investigate why LLM judges diverge from human consensus and exhibit inconsistent alignment across models, we analyze their prediction behavior using confusion matrices (Fig. 2 ), using the zero-shot setting as an example. The results show that most disagreements occur in the Functionally Almost Correct category, where borderline cases are frequently misclassified as either correct or incorrect, suggesting that LLM judges lack the sensitivity needed to reliably evaluate borderline functional equivalence. The matrices also reveal different evaluation tendencies across models. DeepSeek exhibits the most balanced predictions with most mass on the diagonal, which explains its highest correlation with human annotations. In contrast, Claude models and GPT-4.1 tend to be stricter by downgrading correct Scripts to almost correct, while GPT-3.5 shows a strong conservative bias by rarely predicting correct samples. This suggests that LLM judges differ in both accuracy and strictness, meaning that model selection plays a critical role depending on whether conservative or balanced evaluation is desired.

paragraphs.en: Traditional lexical metrics such as BLEU and ROUGE, while useful for source code, often fail to capture the functional equivalence of generated scripts. Our findings indicate that LLM-based judges can bridge this “semantic gap” by evaluating the intent and logic of a generated Script rather than its character-level overlap. While human expert annotation remains the “gold standard” for reliability, it is unscalable and expensive. Although LLM judges do not yet match human reliability, their substantial alignment with human annotations suggests they can serve as a scalable and cost-effective evaluation method for workflow automation tasks.

paragraphs.en: Threats to internal validity concern whether the study accurately reflects cause–effect relationships. To mitigate this, we fixed random seeds across experiments, used consistent data splits to support reproducibility. To mitigate this, we used uniform prompting templates and documented all configurations to support replication.

paragraphs.en: Threats to construct validity concern whether our evaluation truly measures the intended concepts. paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduced FLOWSTEP , a framework designed to improve the recommendation of GitHub Actions workflow steps by explicitly modeling the heterogeneity between Actions and Scripts . By leveraging a “divide-and-conquer” architecture, we integrated a RoBERTa-based classifier for step-type prediction, contrastive learning for reusable Action selection, and Large Language Models for project-specific Script generation. Our evaluation demonstrates that this step-type-aware formulation substantially outperforms existing baselines. As commonly used metrics do not fully capture the correctness of generated scripts, we further validated whether LLMs can serve as reliable evaluators. Our results show that there is substantial alignment between human annotations and LLMs’ evaluations, indicating a promising path in this direction.
paragraphs.zh: 在本工作中，我们提出了 FLOWSTEP，一个通过显式建模 Actions 与 Scripts 之间的异构性来改进 GitHub Actions 工作流步骤推荐的框架。 通过采用“分而治之”的架构，我们集成了基于 RoBERTa 的分类器用于步骤类型预测、对比学习用于可复用 Action 的选择，以及大语言模型用于项目特定的 Script 生成。 我们的评估表明，这种感知步骤类型的建模方式显著优于现有基线方法。 由于常用指标无法充分衡量生成 Script 的正确性，我们进一步验证了大语言模型能否作为可靠的评估者。 我们的结果显示，人工标注与大语言模型的评估之间存在高度一致性，这表明该方向是一条有前景的路径。

paragraphs.en: Although FLOWSTEP improves workflow step generation accuracy, it relies solely on the workflow specification and does not exploit repository-specific information. As future work, we plan to investigate an agentic CI system that actively explores the target repository to leverage project-specific context for more accurate workflow generation and correction. We also plan to integrate vulnerability detection and security analysis to generate CI/CD workflows that are both functionally correct and secure by design.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管 FLOWSTEP 提高了工作流步骤生成的准确性，但它仅依赖工作流规范，没有利用代码仓库特定的信息。 作为未来工作，我们计划研究一种智能体化的 CI 系统，主动探索目标代码仓库，利用项目特定的上下文来实现更准确的工作流生成与修正。 我们还计划集成漏洞检测与安全分析，以生成在功能上正确且在设计上安全的 CI/CD 工作流。
